test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 28 Jan 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What is the name of the Company which is responsible for Bhopal tragedy in 1984 that happened due to accidental leakage of Methyl Isocyanate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Union Carbide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhopal Gas Tragedy**

 
 
• The **Union Carbide India Limited (UCIL) pesticide plant in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh,** India, experienced a chemical accident on the night of **December 2-3, 1984**, which is also known as the **"Bhopal disaster" or "Bhopal gas tragedy."**
 
• The industrial disaster is regarded as the **worst in human history**.
 
• **Methyl isocyanate (MIC)** gas was inhaled by more than **500,000 persons**.
 
• The little settlements close to the facility were affected by the very hazardous chemical that had spread there. 
 
• There were **2,259 confirmed immediate deaths**.
 
• The family members of the** 5,743,666 injured victims and the 3,787 victims** killed in the gas spill received compensation from the **Madhya Pradesh government in 2008**. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• According to a federal affidavit in 2006, there were **558,125 injuries as a result of the leak, including 38,478 temporary partial impairments and roughly 3,900 seriously and permanently disabling injuries**.
 
• Others claim that** 8,000 people **perished within two weeks, and another 8,000 or more have since passed away from illnesses linked to gas. 
 
• **Union Carbide Corporation (UCC) held a majority of ownership in UCIL**, the company that owned the factory, while Indian Government-controlled banks and the Indian public each held a 49.1 per cent stake.
 
• UCC settled legal claims arising from the disaster in **1989 by paying $470 million** (equivalent to $871 million in 2020).
 
• **Warren Anderson, the CEO of UCC **at the time of the tragedy, was the target of numerous civil and criminal actions brought in the United States against him between 1986 and 2012.
